profile.summary: LucaOne is a biological foundation model that reads nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) and protein sequences with one shared model. Given a sequence and its type, it returns an embedding: a matrix with one vector per residue or a single vector for the whole sequence. These embeddings are used as inputs to downstream models for sequence-level or residue-level classification and regression.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: title, TimeLine 2025/12/31; LucaOneApp README: embedding methods and parameters

summary_quotes.text: LucaOne: Generalized Biological Foundation Model with Unified Nucleic Acid and Protein Language.
seq_type: type of input sequence: `gene` or `prot`, `gene` for nucleic acid(DNA or RNA), `prot` for protein.
embedding_type: `matrix` or `vector`, output the embedding matrix or [CLS] vector for the entire sequence, recommend: matrix.
You can fine-tune the model for both sequence-level and token-level classification or regression tasks.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: LucaOne (also called LucaGPLM) is a transformer encoder over a joint vocabulary of nucleotides and amino acids. The published checkpoint has a masked language model head, which the developers describe as for pre-training and sequence recovery; the full set of pretraining tasks is described in the paper, which was not read. The published default checkpoint has 20 layers, hidden size 2560, 40 attention heads and a 39-token vocabulary, with no absolute position embeddings. Each input is marked as gene (DNA or RNA) or prot. The output is the last hidden layer: per-token vectors including [CLS] and [SEP], which can be pooled to one vector by mean, [CLS] or trainable attention pooling. Long sequences are split into overlapping fragments and the embeddings merged.
sections.source_locator: model card: Usage; config.json; LucaOneApp README: embedding methods, notes

quotes.text: # last hidden matrix as embedding matrix: [batch_size, seq_len + 2, hidden_size]
For long sequences, LucaOne will do overlapped fragments in the sequence for embedding and finally merge them into a completed embedding matrix.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Checkpoints are named by training step. The README recommends lucaone at step 36000000, 17600000 or 5600000 for both nucleic acid and protein, lucaone-gene at step 36800000 for DNA and RNA only, and lucaone-prot at step 30000000 for protein only. The original code downloads them from the developers' FTP server by --llm_type, --llm_version and --llm_step. Since 2025 they are also on Hugging Face under LucaGroup, loaded with the lucaone package (version 1.1.1 for the card read). A result should name the checkpoint and step, the route (FTP code or Hugging Face) and the Hugging Face revision; this page read LucaOne-default-step36M at revision f0d2807e.

strengths.text: Long sequences are handled by overlapping fragments, and the code falls back to CPU when GPU memory runs out.

quotes.text: LucaOne will do overlapped fragments in the sequence for embedding
If the GPU memory is not enough to process the longer sequence, it will use the CPU for embedding, so the speed will be reduced.

strengths.text: Weights are on Hugging Face with standard transformers classes for embedding, masked language modelling and classification, and the pretraining data is deposited in a public archive.

quotes.text: **Hugging Face Native**: Full support for `AutoModel`, `AutoModelForMaskedLM`, `AutoModelForSequenceClassification`, `AutoModelForTokenClassification`, `AutoConfig`, and `AutoTokenizer`.

limitations.text: It is large, at about 1.58 billion parameters for the default checkpoint, and the developers advise a large-memory GPU such as an A100 or H100 for long sequences.

run_guide.summary: Install the lucaone package with the pinned tokenizers and transformers versions, load LucaOne-default-step36M from Hugging Face and embed a short nucleotide sequence.
prerequisites: Python with pip. The original repository uses Python 3.9.13; the model card does not state a Python version.
A GPU is used if available, otherwise CPU. The developers advise a large-memory GPU such as an A100 for long sequences.
Weights are MIT licensed on the model card; code is Apache-2.0. The weights are not gated.

steps.title: Embed a nucleotide sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
import lucaone
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel, TrainingArguments, Trainer

# model_id
model_id = "LucaGroup/LucaOne-default-step36M"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    model_id,
    trust_remote_code=True,
    force_download=True
)

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
    model_id,
    task_level="token_level",
    task_type="embedding",
    trust_remote_code=True,
    force_download=True
)

# device
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model.to(device)
model.eval()

# nucleotide sequence
nucleotide_sequence = "ATGCGTACGTTAGC"
nucleotide_inputs = tokenizer(
    nucleotide_sequence,
    # note: gene sequence(for DNA or RNA), seq_type must be 'gene'
    seq_type="gene",
    return_tensors="pt",
    add_special_tokens=True
)
new_nucleotide_inputs = {}
for item in nucleotide_inputs.items():
    new_nucleotide_inputs[item[0]] = item[1].to(device)
nucleotide_inputs = new_nucleotide_inputs

with torch.no_grad():
    nucleotide_outputs = model(**nucleotide_inputs)
    # last hidden matrix as embedding matrix: [batch_size, seq_len + 2, hidden_size]
    nucleotide_last_hidden = nucleotide_outputs.last_hidden_state
    # mean pooling
    mean_nucleotide_embedding = nucleotide_last_hidden[:, 1:-1, :].mean(dim=1)
print(f"Nucleotide Embedding Shape: {nucleotide_last_hidden.shape}")
print(mean_nucleotide_embedding)
PY
steps.explanation: The model card's feature-extraction example, wrapped in a shell heredoc and shortened: the protein half and some intermediate print lines are left out. Use seq_type="prot" for a protein sequence, as the card shows.

outputs: The shape of the embedding matrix, [batch_size, seq_len + 2, hidden_size], and the mean-pooled embedding vector.
limitations: These commands were read from the model card and have not been executed by Rewire.
force_download=True downloads the weights again on every run.
For long sequences or batch embedding to files, the developers point to the LucaOneApp repository instead.

notes: The record description says about 170,000 species; this was not confirmed because the paper could not be read (bioRxiv 429 twice, no open Europe PMC text). The Hugging Face listing for LucaGroup shows LucaOne-prot-step38.2M while the README recommends lucaone-prot at step 30000000; worth a human look. LucaVirus and LucaCell checkpoints in the same organisation are separate models.
